purpose: Convert the static PursuitDesk prototype into a production-ready database migration path with tenant-first tables, operational/commercial separation, seed order, rollback rules, validation gates, and backend commands.

sourceFixtures.commercialVaultPolicy: Commercial values, agreements, LOA, negotiation rounds, billing, and forecast facts stay outside frontline Tenders and Projects tables.

migrationFiles.purpose: Create company scope, admin ownership, user access snapshots, inactive-user state, and session shell before any business data.
Load tracker-safe tender and project records without commercial values.
Keep values, agreements, LOA, negotiation, and forecast facts behind explicit management permissions.
Stage workbook data, show validation issues, commit only approved rows, and preserve rollback evidence.
Append allowed and denied sensitive actions with actor, tenant, target, request id, and before or after summary.
USD membership, seat changes, invoices, test checkout, and access-lock state stay separate from operational records.
Capture pilot UAT feedback, blockers, owner workflow, retest states, decisions, and sponsor exports.
Hold evidence pack pointers, management report exports, and generated weekly snapshots.
Add query paths after base tables so filters, search, exports, and audits stay fast under tenant scope.
Store count parity, redaction, tenant isolation, import dry-run, rollback, and smoke proof expectations.

tableOwnership.rule: Blocks cross-company data before any route or service can read records.
The frontline Tenders and Projects sheets read only this layer.
Management-only facts stay outside tracker routes and exports.
Excel migration is observable, reversible, and auditable.
Sensitive reads, denials, imports, billing, and membership changes become proof.
USD pricing and membership state are isolated from pursuit data.
Pilot feedback becomes a release-quality backlog, not loose notes.
Management packs can be rebuilt from governed data instead of screenshots.

seedOrder.acceptance: Create CapSa demo company and base tenant settings before users.
Create Operations User, Pursuit Manager, Control Admin, and membership plans.
Admin, editor, viewer, inactive, and denied-role cases become fixture users.
Tracker-safe records load without commercial fields.
Values, LOA, negotiation, and forecast facts load only after record ids exist.
Source workbooks become dry-run, quarantine, and rollback fixtures.
Allowed and denied sensitive events create proof coverage.
USD test-mode membership and seat events prove commercial access locks.
Pilot blockers, retest states, sponsor exports, and decisions become persistent fixtures.
Counts, redaction, access, import, rollback, and report expectations are stored for CI.

rollbackRules.detail: Take a tenant-scoped backup or restore point before any migration commit.
Every migration file needs a safe down path or a documented irreversible decision.
Import batches must be reversible by batch id without touching another tenant.
Commercial fact writes roll back only through vault events, not tracker updates.
Audit events are never deleted; rollback writes reversal events instead.
Invoices and billing events are cancelled or reversed, not removed.
Fixture seeds can run repeatedly without duplicating users, records, or invoices.
Staging restore must be rehearsed before the first customer pilot.

validationGates.test: Imported operational, commercial, audit, feedback, and billing counts match the fixture manifest.
Every migrated row has company_id and rejects cross-tenant reads through route tests.
Tracker queries and exports return no value, agreement, invoice, LOA, or negotiation fields.
Commercial facts can be joined to records only through authorized insight routes.
Dry-run, commit, rollback, and quarantine totals reconcile to source workbook inventory.
Allowed and denied reads write audit events with request id and actor context.
High-use filtered lists, search, calendar, audit, and billing queries use planned indexes.
A tenant fixture can restore into staging and pass smoke tests within the release window.

migrationCommands.purpose: Run local migration files in order
Load tenant, users, records, vault, imports, audit, billing, and feedback fixtures
Compare table counts against fixture manifest
Assert tracker-safe queries hide commercial fields
Stage workbook rows without live writes
Reverse the last committed import batch
Export sensitive allowed and denied action evidence
Restore latest fixture backup into staging clone

dataContracts.access: Insight, commercial, management, and admin roles only

nonNegotiableRules: Every table that belongs to a customer carries company_id.
Tenders and Projects routes never expose commercial vault fields.
Commercial fields are joined only through authorized insight or management routes.
Import dry-run never writes live records.
Rollback is rehearsed before live pilot data.
Billing events are reversed, not deleted.
Seed fixtures are idempotent and safe to rerun.
